title: Pulling in fixes for memory leaks in SOME/IP and Signal-PDU

notes.body:
added 3 commits
  • 1fe6417e - 1 commit from branch wireshark:release-3.6
  • 9f0944e2 - SOME/IP: code cleanup to reduce memory leaks
  • 48ddde1d - SIGNAL-PDU: Fixing memory leak in Signal List UAT
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/7393/diffs?diff_id=436912001&start_sha=0b7ad22771b7e803fa55b7f07cc496d747268fea)
I couldn't merge this branch: CI failed!
I am not sure what to do. Is this a bug in the ABI check?

It does seem like the ABI check build is using gcc 11 which hits this issue https://github.com/lvc/abi-dumper/issues/33

Which is fixed in the current Git (pending 1.3) release of abi-check but not in the released 1.2 version:
https://github.com/lvc/abi-dumper/issues/34

https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2041550
This pipeline from two days ago uses gcc-9 in the build, and didn't trigger the issue. https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/jobs/2701382692

That other build is based on Ubuntu focal, which uses gcc-9. I am slightly confused because the container was supposedly moved to jammy (gcc-11) two months ago: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark-containers/-/commit/c8994e3e56275b2eea771a6772e16bbc2171ae8a
@geraldcombs can you take a look? It seems like the ABI check is broken on the latest container after the switch to Ubuntu jammy (22.04)
The container was reverted to focal now, as this is an upstream issue. I restarted the pipeline and it should work.
